name: Parallel AI
summary: AI agent platform for sales, marketing and support: build AI employees on every major model, run Smart Lists for lead generation and enrichment, and schedule content and support agents from one place.
best_for: teams that want the sales, content and support agents in one place and will genuinely use the lead engine -- that half is priced per result, gets cheaper in bulk, and a lookup that finds nothing costs nothing
skip_if: you need a bill you can forecast, because the platform credits that power every AI action carry no published per-action rate -- or you only need one of the four things it does, where a dedicated tool costs less than $99 a month
honest_knock: The free tier is genuinely free -- 50 credits a month, no card -- and it is the only way to answer the question the pricing page leaves open. Data credits are priced per unit, but platform credits are not: nowhere does the page say what a content run, an agent conversation or an outreach step costs, and those are the actions the plan is sold on. So spend those 50 credits on the workflow you would actually buy this for and read Usage & Billing, which tracks consumption by feature, model and timestamp. Until you have that number, 2,000 credits a month is a quantity without a unit.

pricing.notes: (read on 11 September 2026 on parallellabs.app/pricing, which stamps itself 'Last updated: 2026-08-18') The meter is credits, and there are two separate pools. Plan credits come with the subscription: Pay As You Go is $0 with 50 credits a month and no card, Entrepreneur $99 a month for 2,000 credits and 2 companies, Business $297 for 9,000 credits and 10 companies, and Enterprise is quote-only with SSO, on-premise deployment and dedicated support. Data credits are a different pool, bought once and never expiring, and they are the only part of the product priced per action: 1 data credit per lead or contact returned, 2 per matched enrichment lookup through the API or an agent, and a lookup that finds nothing is free. They run $25 for 500 down to $175 for 5,000, so between 5.0 and 3.5 cents a lead. The two pools expire differently, and the page says so in two places that sit far apart: plan credits 'reset on the 1st of each month', while purchased credit packs and data credits never expire. What the page never says is how many PLATFORM credits an action costs. Content generation, an agent conversation and an outreach step are all simply 'credits' with no published rate, so the 2,000 on Entrepreneur is a quantity without a unit until you have run your own work through it. Per credit the tiers differ by a third: 5.0 cents on Entrepreneur against 3.3 on Business, which is three times the price for four and a half times the credits. Running out has a tier-shaped answer -- the FAQ offers extra credit packages on the Business plan and the Pay-As-You-Go card offers top-ups, but Entrepreneur sits between them with no stated top-up route, so the $99 tier's answer to an empty meter appears to be the $297 one. Seats do not add capacity: every seat in a company shares one monthly pool, and extra seats are $15 a month ($12 annual). The add-ons are where the bill can outgrow the plan -- an extra company is $20 a month ($16 annual), an extra white-label instance $50, and anonymous website pixel identification runs $75, $250 or $500 a month for 500, 2,000 or 5,000 resolutions. On the free tier the limits are real: a 200k context window against 1M on every paid plan, 30 days of chat history instead of unlimited, no App Builder, and model access listed as 'Limited' with response times 'limited on bandwidth and availability'. Inside the app on 21 October 2026 the plan screen showed $99 and $297 a month on its annual billing tab ('save 20%'), totalling $1,188 and $3,564 a year (we did not read the monthly tab), and the free plan read 'Monthly credits 4 / 50' after an onboarding that cost 4 credits.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on the free Pay As You Go plan, without a card and without connecting a mailbox: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We described a made-up bicycle repair workshop in four fields, with three hard facts (repairs only, no bike sales; open Monday to Friday 09:00 to 17:00; no appointments by phone), and checked what the onboarding built from it.
findings: The whole onboarding, which built a company profile, an ideal customer profile, an AI team, a knowledge base, website agents, first leads, an email sequence, a content plan and sample content in about two minutes, cost 4 credits in 14 requests (Company Search 7 requests / 2 credits, Content Engine 6 / 2, Sequence 1 / 0). The General page then read 'Monthly credits 4 / 50'.

Of our three facts, the profile kept one ('without the sale of retail bicycles'), blurred one into 'standard weekday business hours' and replaced the third with something we never said: 'By operating as a walk-in facility'. It also set the industry to 'Transportation'.

Without asking, it built a list of 16 real people (facility and operations managers at large companies in Amsterdam) around a partnership idea of its own, and enrolled all 16 in a five-email, AI-personalised sequence. The screen says the sequence 'stays paused until you connect a mailbox and turn on sending'; we connected no mailbox and nothing was sent. We did not record the names.

The content plan, in three funnel stages, promised things we never said: 'Our same-day repair policy explained', 'Success stories: Keeping busy local families mobile' and a 'high-speed repair experience'. Our opening hours and the phone rule appeared nowhere, and the blog draft targeted 'bicycle repair shop' at 22,200 estimated searches a month in the US, for a Dutch audience.

It proposed six AI employees (sales, support, an appointment scheduler and SEO among them) and two chat widgets, for sales and support, each with a ready-made script snippet to paste into a site. With no real website given, the knowledge base reported 'We couldn't import pages from your website this time'.

Right after onboarding a subscription screen opened. On its annual billing tab: Pay As You Go $0 (1 company, 1 seat, 50 credits a month), Entrepreneur $99 a month ($1,188 a year, 2 companies, 2,000 credits), Business $297 a month ($3,564 a year, 10 companies, 10 seats, 9,000 credits) and Enterprise on request. The free plan showed 'Data credits per 5-hour window 0 / 0'.
not_tested: Regenerating a single blog or LinkedIn draft, and the credits per run
Whether the email sequence really sends nothing after you connect a mailbox without turning on sending
How the chat widgets do on a real site
What the data credits (0 / 0 on the free plan) unlock
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
